description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. Run against any rewrite of SKILL.md before merging it.

evals.name: coverage-finding-linkage-form
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: an implementation workflow invokes you for a GitHub issue, and the caller reports a recorded coverage finding — a dependency issue closed and merged on paper, but the capability absent, one acceptance criterion shipped stubbed; the finding produced prerequisite issue #131. Question: which linkage line(s) does the PR body get, what happens to the tracked issue when this PR merges, and what must your output report about the linkage?
evals.expected_output: Part of: <full issue URL> plus Blocked by: <prerequisite URL>, never a closing keyword; a body section naming the unmet criteria. The issue stays open — closing is a human decision. The output reports the form emitted so the caller reconciles completion against it.
assertions: The answer links with Part of: (plus Blocked by: naming the prerequisite) and explicitly rejects Closes:/Fixes:/Resolves: for this PR
The answer states the issue stays open on merge and closing it is a human decision once the gap is filled
The answer reports the emitted linkage form back to the caller (and verifies the form post-creation, not just that a link exists)

evals.name: ambiguous-stack-parent-stops
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the caller supplied a required base branch 'feat/api-layer', which exists and is not the repository default. The caller supplied NO parent PR URL. Searching open PRs, you find TWO open PRs whose head branch is exactly 'feat/api-layer' (a duplicate someone opened). Question: what do you do about stack metadata — pick the older PR as parent, treat the base as an integration branch, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Stop. The parent detection is ambiguous (more than one candidate), and the rule is to stop rather than write incorrect metadata — neither guessing a parent nor silently downgrading to integration-base treatment.
assertions: The answer stops rather than proceeding, on the explicit ambiguity rule
The answer does not pick one of the two PRs as the parent by heuristic (age, author, etc.)
The answer does not silently treat the base as an ordinary integration branch (which the no-candidate rule covers, not the ambiguous case)

evals.name: trigger-authorship-and-identity-reporting
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you created and verified the PR through a transport whose writes have been observed authored as a distinct agent account ('acme-bot'). The workflow now expects the repository's automated review trigger ('@codex review'). Question: (a) may the trigger comment be posted through that agent-authored path? (b) after posting the PR and the trigger, your output must report posting identities — how many entries/answers, and may the PR's and the trigger's observations be merged into one since they could share a (transport, credential) pair?
evals.expected_output: (a) No — the trigger must come from the invoking user's own account or the convention silently does not fire; it is the one post exempted from the posting-identity rule. (b) The PR creation and the trigger comment are reported separately, per write kind, even under a shared pair — a merged single answer overwrites one observation with the other.
assertions: The answer refuses to post the trigger through the agent-authored path and requires the invoking user's account, citing that the convention otherwise fails (silently)
The answer reports the PR-creation observation and the trigger-comment observation as separate entries/kinds, never merged into one
The answer notes the trigger comment's entry is the comment-kind evidence the caller's later trigger selection uses (or equivalently that invoking-user entries must be reported too)

evals.name: unverified-renumber-is-substantive
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: after a sibling merged, the PR branch was rebased and a numbered database migration was renumbered from 0011 to 0014 by hand-editing the filename and the index entry. Nobody has run the migration against anything since. The repository has CI that compiles and runs unit tests, but no check that applies migrations. Question: does this push qualify as mechanical (no review re-trigger), and what would it take for it to qualify?
evals.expected_output: Not mechanical, twice over: the renumber is unverified (hand-edited identity fields, never exercised through the apply path), and the repository has no deterministic check that would catch a bad renumber — either alone disqualifies it. To qualify: regenerate through the repo's own generator and verify it applies (scratch-database migrate), and the repo must have a check standing behind it. Until then, treat as substantive and re-trigger review per convention.
assertions: The answer classifies the push as substantive (review re-trigger due), not mechanical
The answer names the verified-to-apply requirement — regenerate via the repo's generator, exercise the apply path — and rejects hand-edited identity fields (compiling/green unit CI is not enough)
The answer notes that with no deterministic check that would catch a bad renumber, the mechanical exemption is unavailable regardless

evals.name: missing-base-and-missing-issue-stop
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Two sub-scenarios. (A) An orchestrator supplied required base branch 'feat/parent-work', but it does not exist in the repository. (B) A workflow (not a direct user) invokes you for an implementation PR but can supply no issue URL at all — the work has no tracked issue. Question: for each, do you create the PR, and if not, what do you do instead?
evals.expected_output: (A) Stop — a supplied base that does not exist is never silently replaced with the default branch. (B) Stop — an implementation PR that cannot be linked to an exact issue is not created; the ad-hoc exception exists only for directly-invoked PRs after the USER confirms there is no issue, which a workflow invocation is not.
assertions: For (A) the answer stops and does not fall back to the default branch
For (B) the answer does not create an orphan implementation PR from a workflow invocation
The answer scopes the no-issue exception to direct user invocation with explicit user confirmation, which does not apply here

evals.name: trigger-comment-carries-no-footer
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you have created and verified the PR and are about to post the repository's automated review trigger, `@codex review`. Questions: (a) what exactly is the body of that comment? (b) does it carry the attribution footer every other authored write carries, and why?
evals.expected_output: (a) `@codex review` and nothing else. (b) No footer. The trigger comment is exempt from the attribution footer for the same functional reason it is exempt from the posting-identity rule: it must read exactly as the convention expects and must come from the invoking user's own account, and when it does not fire it fails silently — nothing errors and the run waits out a review that was never going to arrive. Every other write this skill makes, the PR body included, carries the footer.
assertions: the trigger comment body is just the trigger text, with no footer appended
the answer names the trigger as the one authored write exempt from the footer
the answer keeps the footer on the skill's other writes, such as the PR body

evals.name: pr-body-stays-short-and-signed
evals.prompt: You are executing the create-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you are opening the PR for issue https://github.com/acme/repo/issues/412, implemented over eleven commits, with two approaches tried and abandoned and a CI shard that failed twice along the way. There is no stack parent, no coverage finding, and the repository documents no PR-description style guide of its own. Question: what goes in the body, what does not, and what is the budget?
evals.expected_output: In: the closing linkage line with the full canonical issue URL (`Closes: https://github.com/acme/repo/issues/412`), then background in 2-4 sentences, then the solution and why this one in a paragraph or at most 5 bullets, then the attribution footer. Budget: 300 words of prose above the fold, a ceiling rather than a target; a manual test checklist is exempt but capped at 8 grouped items. Out: the eleven commits, the two abandoned approaches and the CI shard — that is the journey, not the change under review — plus any file-by-file inventory, any narration of what a function now does, and any investigation log. The body states intent; the diff is the content. Depth a reviewer would genuinely want goes in a collapsed <details> block or a commit message. Over budget means cut, never compress whitespace while keeping every fact. Brevity never drops a mandated element — the linkage line, a `Depends on:` line when stacked, the `Part of:`/`Blocked by:` pair under a coverage finding, and a repository template's headings all survive it.
assertions: the body keeps the full-URL closing linkage line
the answer names the 300-word above-the-fold budget and the 2-4 sentence / 5-bullet shape
the eleven commits, abandoned approaches and CI shard are excluded as the journey
no file-by-file inventory, code narration, or investigation log appears
depth is offered as a collapsed details block or a commit message rather than above the fold
the body ends with the Generated by Claude Code attribution footer
